lesson.name: Learn The Grunfeld Defense
lesson.description: Learn the key ideas for both sides in the dynamic Grunfeld Defense.

{Black has played d5 too early. How should White take over the center?} 3. cxd5
{[%wrong There's a better move. Look at your forcing options and try again.] 
[%hint Capture a pawn.]} (3. Nf3 $2 {This transposes back into a main-line
Grunfeld defense or Queen's Gambit. Try again and look for a more forcing way
to punish Black's move order mistake.}) (3. Nc3 $2 {This transposes back into
a main-line Grunfeld defense or Queen's Gambit. Try again and look for a more
forcing way to punish Black's move order mistake.}) (3. g3 $2 dxc4 {Black
reaches a safe Catalan-style position. Try again and look for a more forcing
option.}) 3... Nxd5 {Good start! e4 is playable, but it's more precise to
delay that advance and develop a piece first. How should you do it?} 4. Nf3 {
[%wrong There's a better developing option. Try to find it.] [%hint Develop a
knight to defend the e5-square.]} (4. e4 $5 {This is a good move, but most
strong players prefer to develop a knight first. Where should it go?}) (4. Nc3
$2 Nxc3 {This transposes into a main line Exchange Grunfeld. Try again and
look for a better way to punish Black's incorrect move order.}) (4. Nd2 $2 {
There's a better and more active knight move. Try to find it.}) 4... g6 {
Great move! How should you take over the center?} 5. e4 {[%wrong There's a
stronger move. Try again and look for a useful threat.] [%hint Control the
center and threaten the knight on d5.] Well played! White has a big center and
Black has an uphill struggle to stay in the game.} (5. h3 $5 {This is a good
move, but White usually takes over the center right away. How should you do it?
}) (5. Nc3 $2 Nxc3 {This transposes into normal Grunfeld positions. Try again
and look for a way to take over the center right away.}) *

{What surprising move should Black play to prepare counterplay against the
d4-pawn and possibly prepare an attack on the white queen?} 8... Nfd7 {[%wrong
There's a better attacking option. Try again and look for a useful knight move.
] [%hint Retreat your f6-knight to free the g7-bishop.] Good choice! The
knight will soon reach b6 to force White's queen to move again and black has
typical Grunfeld counterplay against the big white center.} (8... Bxf3 $5 {
This is reasonable, but it's stronger to increase the pressure by releasing
another attacker against the d4-pawn. How should you do it?}) (8... c6 $5 {
This is reasonable, but it's stronger to increase the pressure by releasing
another attacker against the d4-pawn. How should you do it?}) (8... Nbd7 $5 {
This is reasonable, but it's stronger to increase the pressure by releasing
another attacker against the d4-pawn. How should you do it?}) (8... Nc6 $5 {
This is Ok, but it's stronger to free your g7-bishop to target d4. How should
you do it?}) (8... Ne8 $2 9. Rd1 {Knights are typically passive on the edge of
the board. Try to find a stronger move with this piece.}) (8... Nh5 $2 9. Be2 {
Knights are typically passive on the edge of the board. Try to find a stronger
move with this piece.}) *

{How can White win a pawn and enter the sharp Seville Variation?} 12. Bxf7+ {
[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find it and check the hint if you're
stuck.] [%hint Sacrifice a bishop and then win one back on g4.]} (12. Bd3 $5 {
This is reasonable, but try to find a more aggressive move with the bishop.}) (
12. Bb3 $2 cxd4 {Black has a comfortable position. Try again and look for a
more aggressive bishop move.}) (12. fxg4 $2 Nxc4 {Black wins back the piece
with a good position. Try again and look for a strong move to prepare fxg4.}) (
12. Bd5 $2 Bd7 {Black has a comfortable position. Try again and look for a more
aggressive bishop move.}) 12... Rxf7 {Good start! How should you win back the
piece?} 13. fxg4 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a
good capture.] [%hint Capture an undefended piece.] Well played! White has an
extra pawn, although Black has some compensation. This variation was made
famous by several battles between world champions Karpov and Kasparov in their
1987 match.} *

{White has sacrificed an exchange for a dangerous attack, but Black can defend.
How should you make sure that you won't get mated on the a1-h8 diagonal?} 15...
f6 {[%wrong White has a dangerous attack. Try again and look for a better move.
Feel free to check the hint if you're stuck.] [%hint Block the a1-h8 diagonal
with a pawn.]} (15... Bd7 $2 16. Bh6 {White wins back the exchange with a good
position. Try again and look for a way to prevent tactics on the a1-h8
diagonal.}) (15... Bc8 $2 16. Bh6 {White wins back the exchange with a good
position. Try again and look for a way to prevent tactics on the a1-h8
diagonal.}) (15... Rc8 $2 16. Bh6 {White wins back the exchange with a good
position. Try again and look for a way to prevent tactics on the a1-h8
diagonal.}) 16. Bh6 {Good start! How should you keep a material advantage?} Re8
{[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find a good way to save your f8-rook.] 
[%hint Find a safe square for your f8-rook.] Well played! White has attacking
opportunities, but Black should maintain at least even chances with best play.}
(16... Rf7 $2 17. dxe6 {White wins material and attacks the f7-rook. Try again
and look for a better way to save the rook.}) (16... Qb6+ $2 17. Nd4 {White's
active pieces offer more than enough compensation for the sacrificed exchange.
Try again and look for a way to save your rook from danger.}) *

{Black has let White's center pawns advance much too far and world champion
Kramnik played a winning sacrifice. What was his move?} 30. Bxf7+ {[%wrong
There's a better move. Try to find a winning sacrifice.] [%hint Sacrifice your
bishop to decoy the black king away from defending d7.]} (30. fxg5 $5 {White
is doing well, but Kramnik found an even stronger capture. What was his idea?})
(30. Rxh7 $2 c2 {Black's c2-pawn is dangerous. Try again and look for a better
capture.}) (30. f5 $5 {White is doing well here, but Kramnik found a sacrifice
that was even stronger. What was his move?}) (30. d7+ $2 Kxd7 {Black wins a
key pawn. Try again and look for a stronger sacrifice.}) (30. Rd1 $5 {White is
doing well here, but Kramnik found a sacrifice that was even stronger. What
was his move?}) 30... Kxf7 {Great move! Black resigned in Kramnik-Svidler 1998.
What would White play next if the game had continued?} 31. d7 {[%wrong Black
is winning. Try again and look for a way to promote.] [%hint Bring a second
passed pawn to the seventh rank.] Well done! Black can't stop at least one of
White's pawns from promoting.} *

White's big center provides an edge. Try again and look for a way to win
material.}) (9... Ne5 $2 10. Nxe5 {White's big center provides an edge. Try
again and look for a way to win material.}) (9... Nb8 $2 10. Qd2 {White's big
center provides an edge. Try again and look for a way to win material.}) (9...
Qa5 $2 10. Rc1 {White prepares to sacrifice the c3-pawn with a good position.
Try again and look for a more direct move to win material.}) 10. Bd2 {Good
start! How should you win material?} Bxa1 {[%wrong There's a better option.
Try again and look for a strong capture.] [%hint Find the best capture.]} (
10... Bxd2+ $2 11. Qxd2 {White's big center offers good compensation for the
sacrificed pawn. Try again and look for a better capture.}) 11. Qxa1 {Good
move! How should Black keep a material edge?} Nd4 {[%wrong There's a better
move. Try again and look for a way to keep a material advantage.] [%hint Use
your knight to block the long diagonal.]} (11... O-O $2 12. dxc6 {White wins
material. Try again and find a stronger move to keep a material edge.}) 12.
Nxd4 {Good choice! What's next?} cxd4 {[%wrong White wins material. Try again
and look for a good capture.] [%hint Recapture the knight.] Well played! White
doesn't have enough compensation for the sacrificed exchange.} *

{With the rook on b1, White has additional attacking options. Try to find a
way to start a strong attack.} 9. d5 {[%wrong There's a better attacking idea.
Try to find a strong threat.] [%hint Threaten Black's knight with a pawn.]} (9.
Be3 $5 {This is reasonable, but there's a more aggressive attacking option.
Try to find it.}) (9. Bb5 $5 {This is reasonable, but there's a more
aggressive attacking option. Try to find it.}) 9... Bxc3+ {Good start! How
should you escape the check?} 10. Bd2 {[%wrong Illegal] [%hint Develop and
block the check.]} (10. Nd2 $2 Nd4 {Black has an extra pawn and a good
position. Try again and look for a better way out of check.}) (10. Ke2 $2 Nd4+
{Black has an extra pawn and a good position. Try again and look for a better
way out of check.}) (10. Qd2 $2 Bxd2+ {Black wins the queen. Try again and
look for a better way to block the check.}) 10... Bxd2+ {Nice choice! How
should you recapture?} 11. Qxd2 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and
look for a good capture.] [%hint Recapture and develop your queen.] Well
played! White's strong center and Black's weakened kingside offer more than
enough compensation for the sacrificed pawn.} (11. Kxd2 $2 Bg4 {It's too early
to develop the king. Try again and look for a better capture.}) (11. Ke2 $2 Bh6
{Black wins material. Try again and look for a good capture.}) (11. Nxd2 $2 Nd4
{It's better to develop when you recapture. How should you do it?}) *

{What's the best way for White to get out of check?} 11. Bd2 {[%wrong There's
a better way out of check. Try to find it.] [%hint Develop a piece and
threaten the black queen. It's OK to sacrifice the a2-pawn.]} (11. Kf1 $2 Qxa2
{White can't castle and Black has an extra pawn. Try again and look for a
better way out of check.}) (11. Qd2 $5 {This is reasonable, but it's stronger
to develop another piece and sacrifice the a-pawn. How should you do it?}) (11.
Nd2 $2 Bxd4 {Black wins material. Try again and look for a better way out of
check.}) (11. Rb4 $2 Qxb4+ {Black wins material. Try again and look for a
better way out of check.}) 11... Qxa2 {Good start! How should White continue
to develop?} 12. O-O {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for
a way to secure your king.] [%hint Castle your king to safety.] Well played!
White has a big center and a lead in development. Black will have to play
accurately to show that the extra pawn was worth the hassle.} (12. Ra1 $2 Qe6 {
White doesn't have enough compensation for the lost pawn. Try again and look
for a way to secure your king.}) *
